content: 1. Administer 8 mg/25 mcg of the medication orally once daily from days 1 to 24, followed by 75 mg of ferrous fumarate orally once daily from days 25 to 28. Exercise caution in patients with renal impairment and monitor blood pressure. Do not use in patients with hepatic impairment. This regimen is not recommended for premenarchal individuals. 2. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors, such as ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir, or ethinylestradiol, increases fezolinetant’s AUC and peak plasma concentration. This is contraindicated due to the potential for increased toxicity. 3. Clinical trials have shown ALT elevations greater than 5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), including some cases exceeding 20 times ULN, when ethinylestradiol is co-administered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, with or without dasabuvir. Discontinue ethinylestradiol-containing medications before initiating these hepatitis C combination drugs. Ethinylestradiol-containing medications can be restarted approximately two weeks after completing the hepatitis C drug regimen. 4. Co-administration of tranexamic acid and ethinylestradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. Avoid using tranexamic acid with combination hormonal contraceptives. 5. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 6. Ethinylestradiol reduces the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use. Anastrozole should not be administered with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 7. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor for therapeutic loss if co-administration is unavoidable, and adjust doses as needed. 8. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 9. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinylestradiol. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 10. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing absorption. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Studies in animals have shown significant reductions in plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies are not available. 11. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with hormonal contraceptives may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 12. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with hormonal contraceptives may result in decreased concentrations and loss of efficacy. Brigatinib may cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 14. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 15. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, making concomitant use not recommended. Use alternative non-oral contraceptive methods for females of childbearing potential. 16. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 17. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 21. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 23. Ethinylestradiol reduces the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Advise women to use nonhormonal contraceptives during treatment and for one week after discontinuing elagolix. 24. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of eltrombopag by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least four hours. 25. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 26. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by an unspecified mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. 27. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with hormonal contraceptives may result in decreased concentrations and loss of efficacy. Encorafenib may cause fetal harm. Advise women of childbearing potential to use highly effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 28. Ethinylestradiol reduces the efficacy of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 29. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control. 31. Ethinylestradiol reduces the efficacy of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Exemestane should not be administered with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 32. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by an unspecified mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of fedratinib with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors. 33. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
